newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Little progress in De Beers talks - union.
newsitem.headline: Little progress in De Beers talks - union.

text.p: Four rounds of wage talks between De Beers and South Africa's National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) have made little progress, the union said on Wednesday.
But a union statement said negotiations would resume on May 7.
"There has been no agreement on wage increases. The union demands a 17.5 percent pensionable wage increase across the board, while the company is offering 6.5 percent," it said.
Issues relating to housing, job grading, provident and pension funds had been sent to working committees and other contentious items had already been referred to arbitration, the NUM added.
Negotiations between De Beers and the union, which represents about 5,000 workers at the company's mines, began last month.
South Africa's year-on-year consumer price inflation rate for March was 9.6 percent.
Last year the two sides reached an agreement for pay rises ranging between 9.25 and 9.5 percent.
